implementation_order: Retain measured building coordinates and current ground datum.
Trace pale perimeter and central red path; connect component entry thresholds with short local joins.
Preserve large uninterrupted lawn and add Ryan garden bed/steps.
Add tree masses and low planting, avoiding duplicate trees already owned by components.
Audit matched 9 s, 18 s, 137 s, 139 s and official-aerial viewpoints.
limitations: Four manually interpreted corner/entry picks establish a ground-plane homography. Algebraically zero fit residual is not survey accuracy. Independent older path checks differ by 2.27 and 3.88 m; inferred ground positions remain approximate.
The 139 s upper-image building is Alumni Chapel at the west end, not Ryan. Ryan east end uses separate 9/18 s imagery and its local measured frame.
Do not apply a ground-plane homography to roof or crown pixels as though they were ground coordinates. Trees here are interpreted trunk/crown proposals with explicit uncertainty.
No classified-LiDAR tree heights or current planting survey was recovered in this first stage.
Raw Chapel footprint predates its modeled south addition. Avoid landscape conflicts with the current generated addition, not only the historical source ring.
Existing paving materials changed: 2021 orthophoto/OSM dark service surfaces cannot override 2026 pale pedestrian paving.
Entries and retaining walls are engineered geometry; building-underfoot DEM interpolation must not become floor/step geometry.

engineered_terraces.evidence: Photo-interpreted terrace extent, joined to the actual Athey central north door (U37, measured V=-5.0983). Native review found the initial research polygon ended short. The threshold height is the existing door block bottom, not under-building DEM.
